issues.legal_issue: A court cannot use its inherent powers to reconsider the correctness of an appealable remand order that an aggrieved party did not appeal.
material_facts: The first appellate court made an appealable remand order deciding issues concerning the court’s jurisdiction and the effect of property vesting in the State.
The defendants did not appeal the remand order.
After the case proceeded on remand, the High Court used its inherent powers to reconsider the effect of the property vesting and held that the claimant had lost title.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not reconsider the correctness of the unappealed remand order; the bar in Section 105(2) applied, and Section 151 did not permit the High Court to exercise appellate power.
issues.legal_principle: Section 105(2) precludes a party that does not appeal an appealable remand order from later disputing its correctness. Section 151 cannot be used to do what the Code prohibits, where the Code provides a specific remedy that the party neglected to use, or to exercise appellate power. The order was appealable under Order 43, having been made under Order 41, Rule 23. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: appeal_from_post_remand_decree and prior_remand_order_appealable and prior_remand_not_appealed and reviewing_court_reconsidered_remand_merits

predicates.appeal_from_post_remand_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree made after a case was remanded.
predicates.prior_remand_order_appealable: A court made an earlier remand order that could be appealed.
predicates.prior_remand_not_appealed: The party seeking to challenge the remand order did not appeal it.
predicates.reviewing_court_reconsidered_remand_meri: A reviewing court reconsidered the correctness of the earlier remand order.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a post-remand decree involves an appealable remand order that was not appealed, the reviewing court does not reexamine that order’s correctness.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who may have owned property when it vested in the State retains an interest in establishing that ownership if it affects entitlement to compensation, and the State should be joined so the parties’ rights can be determined.
material_facts: The suit properties vested in the State under an abolition law while the suit was pending.
The claimant asserted that he was the full owner of the properties when the law came into force.
It was conceded that a person proved to have been the owner at that time would be entitled to compensation under the law.
The State was not a party to the appeal, and the High Court held that the claimant had lost his rights in the properties.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s possible entitlement to compensation meant that he remained interested in establishing his ownership at the time of vesting. The High Court’s decree was set aside, and the case was remanded with a direction to join the State and determine the rights of all parties.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the rule in Himatrao v. Jaikishandas and Others, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 815. Where property has vested in the State but a claimant’s ownership at vesting may determine entitlement to compensation, that claimant remains interested in establishing ownership; the State should be joined so the parties’ rights can be finally determined.

rule.if: appeal_concerns_property_vested_in_state and claimant_ownership_at_vesting_disputed and ownership_affects_compensation and state_not_party

predicates.appeal_concerns_property_vested_in_state: The appeal concerns property that vested in the State.
predicates.claimant_ownership_at_vesting_disputed: A claimant asserts ownership of the property when it vested, and that ownership is disputed.
predicates.ownership_affects_compensation: The claimant’s ownership at vesting affects whether the claimant is entitled to compensation.
predicates.state_not_party: The State in which the property vested is not a party to the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns property vested in the State, disputed ownership at vesting affects compensation, and the State is absent, the State is joined and all parties’ rights are determined.
